title: Sustained Windows Page File Utilization
exclusions: Reports an individual Windows `Paging File(*)\% Usage` instance whose sampled percentage is strictly above 90% for three consecutive one-minute buckets, with the newest bucket in the scheduled closed slice. Microsoft states that even 100% page-file usage does not by itself indicate a performance problem unless system commit and modified-page-list conditions also support pressure. The rule therefore does not prove page-file exhaustion, low physical memory, active paging I/O, disk bottleneck, memory leak, process failure, commit-limit breach, crash-dump insufficiency, or root cause. It excludes `_Total`, `% Usage Peak`, missing/invalid values, samples outside 0–100, gaps, other Memory/Paging counters, and hosts without the configured input. The 90% threshold, three-minute persistence, one-minute interval and five-minute close delay are local starting policies. Dynamic system-managed growth changes the denominator. Missing/duplicate samples, localized counter-name mismatch and late data are source-health conditions. No page-file, RAM, process or reboot setting is changed.
evidence: Retain the version-controlled `windows_pagefile_sustained_utilization` search, schedule, ACL and results; each row with host, page-file instance, three sample times/counts/min/average/latest percentage, source metadata and index time; raw Perfmon events; exact inputs.conf/deployment-app version and English-counter setting; expected-host/instance, interval, delay and duplicate health; Windows page-file configuration and current allocated sizes; correlated commit, Available MBytes, Modified Page List Bytes, page I/O and disk-free/latency data; incident/change/capacity decisions, exception approval, alert delivery and dated positive, negative, gap, boundary, dynamic-growth and upgrade tests. This documentation review sampled no counter, ran no SPL, changed no page file and produced no runtime evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Under absolute test bounds, ingest `Perfmon:Paging_File` samples for host `mem-lab-01`, object `Paging File`, counter `% Usage`, instance `C:\pagefile.sys`, at epochs 60 seconds apart with numeric Value 91.0, 92.0 and 93.0; place the third bucket in the newest eligible five-minute period. Expect exactly one row with `sample_count=3`, `minimum_usage_pct=91`, `average_usage_pct=92`, `latest_usage_pct=93`, and a 120-second first-to-last span.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows independently for values 90/95/99 (strict threshold fails), 91/92 with only two samples, 91/92/93 separated by a missing minute, Value 101 or nonnumeric, counter `% Usage Peak`, instance `_Total`, wrong object/source/source type, newest excluded five minutes, stale latest sample, and duplicated samples that source health identifies. Also test a system-managed page file growing between samples: the rule may clear because the percentage denominator changed, and correlation must retain the size/configuration change.

dataSources: Windows Performance Counter `\Paging File(*)\% Usage`, the current percentage of each page-file instance in use; optionally collect `% Usage Peak` for context, not as the primary predicate. Configure a Splunk Windows perfmon input with Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) to deployment-choice `index=perfmon`, local stanza-derived `sourcetype=Perfmon:Paging_File` (explicitly a deployment convention). Required fields: `_time, _indextime, host, object, counter, instance, Value, source, sourcetype`. Use `useEnglishOnly=true` where supported and validate exact emitted names. Correlate `Memory\% Committed Bytes In Use`, `Available MBytes`, `Modified Page List Bytes`, page input/output and hosting-disk metrics.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) and the Splunk platform Windows perfmon input. A local operations app owns the input contract, analytic, source health, dashboard, fixtures and `windows_pagefile_capacity_exceptions.csv`.
spl:
index=perfmon sourcetype="Perfmon:Paging_File" object="Paging File" counter="% Usage" earliest=-40m@m latest=-5m@m
| eval destination=lower(trim(host)), pagefile_instance=lower(trim(instance)), usage_pct=tonumber(Value)
| where len(destination)>0 AND len(pagefile_instance)>0 AND pagefile_instance!="_total" AND isnotnull(usage_pct) AND usage_pct>=0 AND usage_pct<=100
| bin _time span=1m
| stats avg(usage_pct) AS usage_pct count AS raw_sample_count max(_indextime) AS last_indextime values(source) AS observed_sources values(sourcetype) AS observed_sourcetypes by destination pagefile_instance _time
| sort 0 destination pagefile_instance _time
| streamstats window=3 current=true count AS sample_count min(usage_pct) AS minimum_usage_pct avg(usage_pct) AS average_usage_pct earliest(_time) AS first_sample_time latest(_time) AS latest_sample_time by destination pagefile_instance
| eventstats max(_time) AS newest_instance_sample by destination pagefile_instance
| where _time=newest_instance_sample AND _time>=relative_time(now(),"-10m@m") AND sample_count=3 AND latest_sample_time-first_sample_time=120 AND minimum_usage_pct>90
| eval latest_usage_pct=round(usage_pct,2), minimum_usage_pct=round(minimum_usage_pct,2), average_usage_pct=round(average_usage_pct,2), threshold_pct=90, required_consecutive_samples=3, sample_interval_seconds=60, close_delay_minutes=5, analytic_interpretation="sustained high usage of one allocated page-file instance; correlate commit, modified list, physical memory and disk; not proof of exhaustion", use_case="UC-1.2.69"
| table destination pagefile_instance first_sample_time latest_sample_time sample_count raw_sample_count minimum_usage_pct average_usage_pct latest_usage_pct threshold_pct required_consecutive_samples sample_interval_seconds close_delay_minutes observed_sources observed_sourcetypes last_indextime analytic_interpretation use_case
| sort 0 -latest_usage_pct destination pagefile_instance
description: Reports the latest row per host and non-total page-file instance when three gap-free one-minute `% Usage` buckets are each above 90% in the closed search slice. It reports minimum, average and latest percentage at host/instance grain and explicitly requires memory/commit correlation before diagnosing exhaustion.
value: Persistent high utilization of an allocated page file can identify capacity risk or changing memory demand that merits correlation before applications fail or a hosting disk loses growth headroom. Per-instance, gap-aware results support defensible page-file and RAM planning without treating a single percentage as proof of memory pressure. This improves memory-capacity decisions by separating sustained page-file pressure from a single transient sample.
implementation: Deploy an English-name perfmon input for Paging File `% Usage` at 60 seconds and validate per-file instances and numeric Value. Save `windows_pagefile_sustained_utilization`, run every five minutes over the delayed slice, and alert only on the three-sample condition. Route with asset/service ownership and investigate commit charge/limit, available and modified memory, page-file allocation/growth, page I/O, disk headroom and process demand before changing configuration.
visualization: Operations dashboard `Windows — Page File Utilization`: source/interval/duplicate and expected-instance health first; per-instance usage trend with 90% policy line; current allocated size and disk headroom; correlated committed percentage, Available MBytes, Modified Page List Bytes and page I/O; table matching SPL output; exception expiry and capacity actions. Label the panel “allocated page-file utilization—not exhaustion or paging-rate proof.”
schema: Windows Paging File performance object, % Usage counter, per-page-file instance
dataModelAcceleration: No standard CIM field is claimed as exact parity for per-instance `Paging File\% Usage` with native instance, one-minute continuity and dynamic allocated-size semantics. `swap_used_percent` mappings may collapse instances or represent another platform concept. No `cimSpl` is provided; a metrics-index or summary implementation must preserve host/instance/value, sample timing and raw parity.

knownFalsePositives:
A result reflects real sampled utilization above local policy; benign or non-actionable explanations include:

1. **Crash-dump sizing or intentionally fixed small page file** — a small file can show high percentage while system commit remains safe. Verify page-file purpose/size, dump policy, commit charge/limit, modified list and disk headroom with the platform owner.
2. **System-managed page-file resize** — Windows can grow the allocated file, changing the percentage denominator. Correlate configured/current size, System events, disk free space and timing; do not interpret a falling percentage as workload recovery without size context.
3. **Planned load, backup, compilation, analytics or application warm-up** — temporary committed-memory demand can persist for minutes. Match exact job/change, process private bytes/commit, service SLO, duration and return to baseline.
4. **Failover, restart or cache repopulation** — clustered/application recovery can increase commit temporarily. Validate orchestration ID, node role, process ownership, availability and completion.
5. **New deployment or memory-intensive service** — legitimate growth can exceed a historical page-file design. Correlate release, process commit, host sizing, workload forecast and capacity ticket; sustained use still requires action.
6. **Duplicate or irregular perfmon collection** — overlapping stanzas/forwarders can create duplicate buckets and missing samples can falsify persistence. Repair source ownership and interval health.
7. **Authorized capacity test** — preserve the result and test metrics; suppress duplicate notification only for exact hosts/instances and approved UTC bounds.

**Safe suppression:** apply lookup windows_pagefile_capacity_exceptions.csv after base detection. Require exact `destination,pagefile_instance`, exception ID, numeric inclusive `valid_from_epoch`, exclusive `valid_until_epoch`, owner, approver, change/capacity ticket, purpose and maximum approved percentage/duration. Reject wildcard fleets, `_Total` rules and open-ended dates. Never suppress missing/duplicate/interval health; retain all base results.

The query scans 35 closed minutes and performs host/instance one-minute and three-row streaming aggregation. Measure fleet instance count and prefer metrics indexes only after parity.

detailedImplementation:
## Define the counter contract

Assign Windows performance, application/service, capacity, storage, Splunk collection/content and on-call owners. Inventory each host, service, environment, RAM, page-file mode (system-managed/fixed/none), configured and current allocated file sizes, hosting volume/free-space policy, crash-dump requirement, expected instances, maintenance windows and forwarding path. Restrict detailed process/capacity dashboards with an operations Splunk role.

Microsoft defines `Paging File(*)\% Usage` as the percentage of each page-file instance in use. It is not the paging-I/O rate. Microsoft also states 100% use is not itself a performance problem if system commit has not reached its limit and a significant modified page list is not waiting. The local alert requires strictly above 90% for three consecutive one-minute buckets; this is a triage policy, not a Microsoft limit.

## Configure and validate Perfmon

Deploy Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows from Splunkbase 742. Manage a deployment-app `inputs.conf` stanza:

```ini
[perfmon://Paging_File]
object = Paging File
counters = % Usage;% Usage Peak
instances = *
interval = 60
mode = single
useEnglishOnly = true
index = perfmon
disabled = 0
```

Validate the emitted event contract. `index=perfmon` and stanza-derived `sourcetype=Perfmon:Paging_File` are local choices, not universal vendor defaults. Confirm object `Paging File`, counter `% Usage`, per-file instance names, numeric Value, host, source and one sample each 60 seconds. Exclude `_Total` from the primary rule so each row has a concrete page-file denominator.

Collect correlation counters in separately tested stanzas: `Memory\% Committed Bytes In Use`, `Committed Bytes`, `Commit Limit`, `Available MBytes`, `Modified Page List Bytes`, `Page Reads/sec`, `Page Writes/sec`, `Page Inputs/sec`, and disk free/latency for page-file volumes. Do not call `Pages/sec` page-file I/O; hard faults can read mapped files and executables.

```spl
index=perfmon sourcetype="Perfmon:Paging_File" earliest=-30m
| table _time _indextime host object counter instance Value source sourcetype
| sort 0 host instance _time
```

Compare with **Performance Monitor > Paging File > % Usage** and current Windows page-file configuration. Test fixed and system-managed files, multiple files and a host with no page file.

## Monitor source quality

Build expected-host/instance health for absent/stale samples, interval outside 50–90 seconds, excessive `_indextime-_time`, duplicate host/instance/counter/time, nonnumeric or outside-0–100 values, unknown instances, localization/name drift, disabled stanzas and forwarder backlog. Track configuration/current-size changes because dynamic growth changes the percentage denominator.

Missing samples invalidate a three-minute sequence. Overlapping stanzas can overweight an average even when timestamps match. Repair collection instead of using arbitrary `dedup`. Route page-file-hosting disk free-space risk separately.

## Schedule and understand the SPL

Save as `windows_pagefile_sustained_utilization`, schedule every five minutes and trigger on result count greater than zero. It scans `earliest=-40m@m latest=-5m@m`, leaving five minutes for arrival. The 35-minute history tolerates scheduling while selecting only the newest eligible instance row.

The query validates host/instance and a 0–100 numeric value, bins to one minute and averages duplicate raw samples within a bucket while retaining their count. Ordered `streamstats` computes the last three buckets. The result requires three samples, exactly 120 seconds from first to last, minimum above 90 and a newest sample no older than the final five-minute band. One result means one page-file instance met persistence; it does not mean every page file is high or commit is exhausted.

No CIM query is asserted. A metrics-index implementation can reduce event cost but must preserve object/counter/instance dimensions, sampling time, continuity and parity.

## Validate and operationalize

Replay the exact 91/92/93 fixture and assert all fields. Run each negative independently: boundary 90, two points, gap, invalid values, Peak, `_Total`, wrong source/object, delayed and duplicate data. Test multiple instances, system-managed growth, clock skew, latest/earliest boundaries, host renaming and add-on upgrades. Confirm source-health alerts independently.

Use Windows Performance Recorder/Monitor or an approved disposable workload in a lab to raise committed memory without risking production. Capture page-file allocated-size changes, commit charge/limit, Available MBytes, modified list, page I/O and disk headroom. A synthetic Splunk fixture proves SPL; a lab workload proves collection; neither proves production thresholds.

Dashboard and alert testing must verify ACLs, exact instance drilldown, ticket routing, notification throttle and exception expiry. Alert title: `Sustained page-file utilization <latest_usage_pct>% on <destination>/<pagefile_instance>`.

Analysts verify raw samples and continuity, then compare commit percentage/limit, modified list, available physical memory, page reads/writes, process commit/private bytes, current page-file allocation, system-managed growth, hosting-volume free/latency, workload/change and service impact. Capacity owners decide whether to fix a leak, add RAM, resize/add a page file, relocate storage or change workload. Preserve crash-dump requirements. Never automatically resize page files or terminate processes from this result.

Apply lookup windows_pagefile_capacity_exceptions.csv after detection. Retain base results and source health. Review repeated findings, dynamic size and exception expiry weekly.

## Troubleshoot

- No samples: verify object/counter spelling, `useEnglishOnly`, stanza deployment, forwarder permissions/health, index route and page-file existence.
- Only `_Total`: collect `instances=*` and inspect per-file names; do not silently use aggregate semantics.
- Value exceeds 100/nonnumeric: inspect raw event, locale/extraction and duplicate stanzas.
- High percentage without pressure: expected possibility; inspect commit and modified list per Microsoft guidance.
- Usage drops suddenly: check system-managed growth or restart before calling recovery.
- Gaps prevent alert: repair interval/forwarding; do not weaken continuity without documenting changed semantics.
- Metric/CIM counts differ: audit dimensions, rollups and time alignment; event source remains authoritative until parity.
grandmaExplanation: We watch each Windows page file for several minutes of very high use. That is a reason to check memory and disk capacity, but the percentage alone does not mean the computer has run out of memory.
hardware: Windows hosts exposing the Paging File performance object and at least one page-file instance through a validated perfmon input. Hosts without a page file, localized/untranslated counters, non-Windows swap, container-only memory and systems collected only through another metric schema require separate analytics.
